questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are forty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any working should be done in this booklet. questions.questionText: What will reduce the systematic errors when taking a measurement?

options.A: adjusting the needle on a voltmeter so that it reads zero when there is no potential difference across it
options.B: measuring the diameter of a wire at different points and taking the average
options.C: reducing the parallax effects by using a marker and a mirror when measuring the amplitude of oscillation of a pendulum
options.D: timing 20 oscillations, rather than a single oscillation, when finding the period of a pendulum

questions.questionText: In an experiment to determine the acceleration of free fall g, the time t taken for a ball to fall through distance s was measured. The uncertainty in the measurement of s is estimated to be 2%. The uncertainty in the measurement of t is estimated to be 3%. The value of g is determined using the equation g = 2s . t2 What is the uncertainty in the calculated value of g?

options.A: 1% B 5% C 8% D 11% Space for working –1 –1

questions.questionText: A bicycle brakes so that it undergoes uniform deceleration from a speed of 8ms to 6ms over a distance of 7m. If the deceleration of the bicycle remains constant, what further distance will it travel before coming to rest?

options.A: 7m B 9m C 16m D 21m

questions.questionText: A ball is released from rest above a horizontal surface. It bounces once and is caught. Which graph represents the variation with time t of the velocity v of the ball?

options.A: B C D v v v v 0 0 0 0 0 t 0 t 0 t 0 t Space for working

questions.questionText: A mass on the end of a spring bounces up and down as shown, after being released at time t = 0. distance up 0 time t distance down Which graph shows how the velocity varies with time? velocity up

options.A: 0 0 time t velocity up

questions.questionText: The diagram shows two spherical masses approaching each other head-on at an equal speed u. One is of mass m and the other of mass 2m. 2m m u u Which diagram, showing the situation after the collision, is not consistent with the principle of conservation of momentum?

options.A: B 2m m 2m m u 5 u 2 u u

questions.questionText: A molecule of mass m travelling at speed v hits a wall in a direction perpendicular to the wall. The collision is elastic. What are the changes in the kinetic energy and in the momentum of the molecule caused by the collision? change in change in momentum kinetic energy

The IKAROS satellite has mass 320kg and moves through space using a solar sail of area 20m . The average solar wind pressure is 1.0 × 10 –5 Nm –2 . What is the acceleration of the satellite caused by the solar wind?

The graph shows the momentum of a cyclist over a period of 8.0s. momentum /kgms–1 0 2.0 4.0 6.0 8.0 time/s At time 4.0s, she applies the brakes. What is the resultant force on the cyclist during the period when the brakes are applied?

options.A: 55N B 200N C 270N D 450N Space for working

questions.questionText: A hailstone, initially stationary at the base of a cloud, falls vertically towards the Earth. The diagram shows the magnitudes and directions of the forces acting on the hailstone as it starts to drop. gravitational upthrust U viscous force W force V Which diagram shows the magnitudes and directions of these forces when the hailstone attains a terminal (constant) speed in the air (of uniform density)?

options.A: B W U V W U V C D W U V W U V Space for working

questions.questionText: Four beams of the same length each have three forces acting on them. Which beam has both zero resultant force and zero resultant torque acting?

options.A: B 30N 50N 36N 70N 50cm 30cm 50cm 30cm 90N 106N

questions.questionText: The diagrams show the forces acting on different bodies. Which body cannot be in equilibrium?

options.A: B

questions.questionText: A car travelling with speed 28ms leaves a motorway on an exit road. The end of the exit road is 22m higher than the motorway. If only the force of gravity is considered, what will be the speed of the car at the end of the exit road? –1 –1 –1 –1

options.A: 7.3ms B 19ms C 21ms D 24ms Space for working

questions.questionText: A piston in a gas supply pump has an area of 400cm and it moves a distance of 25cm during one stroke. The pump moves the gas against a fixed pressure of 3000Pa. How much work is done by the piston during one stroke?
A transformer has the following input and output. potential current/A difference/V input 11000 28 output 240 1200 What is the efficiency of the transformer?

options.A: 0.94% B 1.0% C 11% D 94% Space for working

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a hydroelectric power station. The reservoir is linked to the turbines by a pipe of uniform cross-sectional area. Water flows from the reservoir, through the pipe and through the turbines at a constant rate. reservoir X turbine house Y Which statement about the change of energy of the water as it moves from X to Y is correct?

options.A: It gains both gravitational potential energy and kinetic energy.
options.B: It loses gravitational potential energy and gains elastic potential energy.
options.C: It loses gravitational potential energy and gains kinetic energy.
options.D: It loses both elastic potential energy and gravitational potential energy. Space for working

questions.questionText: Which row correctly describes the ordering and motion of the molecules in water and in ice when both are at a temperature of 0°C? ordering motion

options.A: a regular pattern molecules in both ice of molecules in ice and water have the but not in water same average speed
options.B: a regular pattern molecules in ice of molecules in ice travel more slowly but not in water than those in water
options.C: a regular pattern molecules in ice of molecules in both travel more slowly ice and water than those in water
options.D: a regular pattern molecules in both ice of molecules in both and water have the ice and water same average speed

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a rectangular block of mass 8.2kg immersed in sea water of density 1.10 × 10 3 kgm –3 . 2.00m 2.20m What is the difference in pressure between the top and bottom surfaces of the block?

A trolley is held at rest between two steel springs. P Q Each spring has an unstretched length of 0.10m. –1 Spring P has spring constant 60Nm . –1 Spring Q has spring constant 120Nm . Spring P has an extension of 0.40m. What is the extension of spring Q?

A lift is supported by two steel cables, each of length 10m and diameter 0.5cm. The lift drops 1mm when a man of mass 80kg steps into the lift. What is the best estimate of the value of the Young modulus of the steel?

The diagram shows an air-filled pipe open at both ends. The length of the pipe is 1.00m and the lower surface of the inside of the pipe is covered with a layer of fine sand. 1.00 m sand When a source of sound of a single frequency is put near one end of the pipe, the air in the pipe is found to resonate and a pattern in the sand shows that a standing wave containing three nodes is formed within the pipe. –1 The speed of sound in air is 330ms . What is the frequency of the sound?

options.A: 330Hz B 495Hz C 990Hz D 1320Hz

questions.questionText: A stationary sound wave is formed in a measuring cylinder by blowing across the top, as shown. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The fundamental frequency of the stationary wave decreases when some water is added to the cylinder.
options.B: The stationary wave in the cylinder is caused by the superposition of two waves moving in opposite directions.
options.C: The stationary wave in the cylinder is polarised.
options.D: The stationary wave will have an antinode at the bottom of the cylinder. Space for working

questions.questionText: Diffraction can be observed when a wave passes an obstruction. The diffraction effect is greatest when the wavelength and the obstruction are similar in size. For waves travelling through air, what is the combination of wave and obstruction that could best demonstrate diffraction?

options.A: microwaves passing a steel post
options.B: radio waves passing a copper wire
options.C: sound waves passing a human hair
options.D: visible light waves passing a gate post

questions.questionText: A health inspector is measuring the intensity of a sound. Near a loudspeaker, his meter records an intensity I. This corresponds to an amplitude A of the sound wave. At another position, the meter gives an intensity reading of 2I. What is the corresponding amplitude of the sound wave? A

options.A: B 2A C 2A D 4A Space for working

A nuclear isotope emits radiation which is detected by a Geiger-Müller tube held at a distance of about 10cm from the radioactive source. The radiation is stopped completely by a 2mm thick sheet of lead. What can be deduced from this information about the emission from the isotope?

options.A: It could be alpha and beta radiation, but not gamma radiation.
options.B: It could be alpha and gamma radiation, but not beta radiation.
options.C: It could be beta and gamma radiation, but not alpha radiation.
options.D: It could be alpha, beta and gamma radiation.

questions.questionText: What remains constant during β-emission from a number of identical nuclei in a substance?

options.A: energy of the β-particles
options.D: proton number of the nuclei Space for working
